### Exploratory Data Analysis

```{r}
load("data_private/airbnb.RData")
bnb_sample_sf <- st_as_sf(bnb_sample, coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326)
```

```{r}
bnb_sample_sf |> 
  ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = state_boundaries) +
  geom_sf()
```

```{r}
us_coastline <- st_transform(us_coastline, 4326)
bnb_sample_sf <- bnb_sample_sf |> 
  mutate(price = exp(log_price),
         host_year = year(host_since)) |> 
  relocate(price, .before = log_price) |> 
  mutate(
    coast_distance = st_distance(geometry, us_coastline),
    coast_distance_km = (as.numeric(coast_distance)/1000)
    ) |> 
  mutate(
    clean_ammenities = str_replace_all(str_to_lower(amenities), "\"", "") |> 
      str_remove_all("\\{|\\}"), 
    ammenities_list = str_split(clean_ammenities, "\\s*,\\s*") |> 
      map(function(x) str_trim(x)),
    has_pool = map_lgl(ammenities_list, function(x) any(str_detect(x, "pools?")))
    ) |> 
  select(-clean_ammenities, -amenities)
```

## Models

### Initial Model with City only

```{r}
lm_bnb_0 <- lm(log(price) ~ city, data = bnb_sample_sf) 
summary(lm_bnb_0)
```

City already explains a large amount of variation in price

### Model with Room type and Host

```{r}
lm_bnb <- lm(log(price) ~ room_type + city + bedrooms + review_scores_rating, data = bnb_sample_sf) 
summary(lm_bnb)
```

R-squared moves up to 0.5644.

#### Adding an Interaction

```{r}
lm_bnb_2 <- lm(log(price) ~ room_type + city*log(coast_distance_km) + bedrooms + review_scores_rating, data = bnb_sample_sf) 
```

```{r}
summary(lm_bnb_2)
```

```{r}
plot(lm_bnb_2)
```

Chicago and DC have `coast_distance_km` that are too high. Including an interaction does not make sense here because the values of `coast_distance_km` do not overlap. Cities without coastal offerings will be removed from the analysis

### Cleaning Raw OSM data

```{r}
clean_osm_data <- function(osm_layer, tag_column, tags, source_type = c("point", "polygon", "multipolygon", "lines"), crs = NULL){
  if(is.null(osm_layer)){
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  source_type <- match.arg(source_type)
  
  if (!is.null(crs)){
    osm_layer <- st_transform(osm_layer, crs = crs)
  }
  
  cleaned_data <- osm_layer |> 
      filter(.data[[tag_column]] %in% tags) |> 
      st_point_on_surface() |> 
      mutate(source = source_type) |> 
      select(
      any_of(c("osm_id", "name", "geometry", "source", tag_column, "bus", "subway", "train", "tram", "ferry", "railway")),
      starts_with("addr:")
    )

  return(cleaned_data)
}


aggregate_osm_data <- function(osm_dataset, tag_column, tags, crs = NULL){
  
  venue_points <- clean_osm_data(osm_dataset$osm_points, tag_column = tag_column, tags = tags, source_type = "point", crs = crs)
  venue_poly <- clean_osm_data(osm_dataset$osm_polygons, tag_column = tag_column, tags = tags, source_type = "polygon", crs = crs)
  venue_multipoly <- clean_osm_data(osm_dataset$osm_multipolygons, tag_column = tag_column, tags = tags, source_type = "multipolygon", crs = crs)
  venue_lines <- clean_osm_data(osm_dataset$osm_lines, tag_column = tag_column, tags = tags, source_type = "lines", crs = crs)
  city_venues <- bind_rows(
    venue_points,
    venue_poly,
    venue_multipoly,
    venue_lines
  )
  return(city_venues)
 
}
```
```{r}
chi_entertainment_clean <- aggregate_osm_data(chi_entertainment_data, "amenity", entertainment_types, crs = 26916) 
chi_culture_clean <- aggregate_osm_data(chi_culture_data, "tourism", culture_types, crs = 26916) 
chi_transport_clean <- aggregate_osm_data(chi_transport_data, "public_transport", transport_types, crs = 26916) 
```

### Preparing OSM Data for KDE

#### Weights for Transport Data


```{r}
transport_methods <- c("bus", "subway", "train", "tram", "ferry", "railway")
```

Manually inspecting the rows with missing `transport_methods` data
```{r}
chi_transport_clean |> 
  st_drop_geometry() |> 
  filter(
    if_all(
      any_of(transport_methods),
      is.na
    )
  )

```

#### `prepare_kde_transport()` function

```{r}

prepare_kde_transport <- function(cleaned_transport_data, transport_methods){
  rail_counts <- cleaned_transport_data |> 
    filter(train == "yes" | subway == "yes") |> 
    group_by(name) |> 
    summarize(
      count = n(),
      geometry = st_point_on_surface(st_union(geometry)),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |> 
  select(name, count, geometry) |> 
  mutate(
    rail_weight = 2 + log1p(count),
    bus_weight = 0,
    tram_weight = 0,
    ferry_weight = 0,
    unknown_weight = 0
    ) 

  other_transport <- cleaned_transport_data |> 
    filter(
      bus == "yes" |
      tram == "yes" |
      ferry == "yes"
    ) |> 
    mutate(
      rail_weight = 0,
      bus_weight = if_else(bus == "yes", 1, 0, missing = 0),
      tram_weight = if_else(tram == "yes", 1, 0, missing = 0),
      ferry_weight = if_else(ferry == "yes", 1, 0, missing = 0),
      unknown_weight = 0
    ) |> 
    select(name, geometry, ends_with("_weight"))

  unknown_transport <- cleaned_transport_data|> 
    filter(
      if_all(
        any_of(transport_methods),
        is.na
      )
    ) |> 
    select(name, geometry) |> 
    mutate(
      rail_weight = 0,
      bus_weight = 0,
      tram_weight = 0,
      ferry_weight = 0,
      unknown_weight = 1
    ) 

    if (
      !all(
        st_crs(rail_counts) == st_crs(other_transport),
        st_crs(rail_counts) == st_crs(unknown_transport)
        )
      ) {
        warning("CRS mismatch between transport datasets")
      }

  transport_kde <- bind_rows(
    rail_counts,
    other_transport,
    unknown_transport
  ) |> 
  mutate(
    total_weight = rail_weight +
            bus_weight +
            tram_weight +
            ferry_weight +
            unknown_weight
  )
  return(transport_kde)
}

```

```{r}
chi_kde_transport_table <- prepare_kde_transport(chi_transport_clean, transport_methods)
```

### KDE for `chi_entertainment_clean`

```{r}
chi_entertainment_clean |> glimpse()
```
```{r}
window <- chi_bbox_buffered |> 
  st_transform(crs = 26916) |> 
  as.owin()
```
```{r}
coords <- chi_entertainment_clean |> 
  st_filter(st_transform(chi_bbox_buffered, 26916)) |> 
  st_coordinates()

pp_entertainment <- ppp(
  x = coords[,1],
  y = coords[,2],
  window = window
)
```
```{r}
plot(pp_entertainment)
```



**Note:** Added the `st_filter()` command because some points were outside the ppp. This needs to be investigated, but it is likely because of st_transform or osm data bringing polygons that are beyond the border. 

```{r}
bw.ppl(pp_entertainment)
```

Likelihood Cross-Validation (`spatstat::bw.ppl`) identified an optimal bandwidth scale near 926m. For model simplicity and interpretability, $\sigma = 1,000\text{m}  (1 \text{km})$ was selected, representing a standard 10-to-12 minute walk for pedestrians."

```{r}
sigma = 1000 #1000 meters based on the existing crs = 26916
kde_entertainment <- density.ppp(
  pp_entertainment,
  sigma = sigma
)
```

```{r}
plot(kde_entertainment)
```


```{r}
raster <- kde_entertainment |> 
  rast() 
  ggplot(data = raster) +
    geom_sf(data = chi_entertainment_clean, alpha = 1) +
  geom_spatraster(data = raster, alpha = 0.5) + 
 
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "magma") +
  annotation_map_tile(alpha = 0.3)+
    
  coord_sf(crs = 26916) 

```
```{r}
#Display KDE
kde_plot <- raster
kde_plot[kde_plot < 1e-6] <- NA  # Make zero-density transparent

ggplot() +
  geom_spatraster(data = kde_plot*100000, alpha = 0.75) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    begin = 0.2,
    option = "magma", 
    na.value = "transparent",
    name = "Venue Density\n(Index x 10^5)"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Chicago Entertainment Venue Density",
    subtitle = "Kernel Density Estimation (σ = 1000m) used in Pricing Model",
    x = "Longitude", y = "Latitude"
  ) +
  annotation_map_tile(alpha = 0.3)+
  coord_sf(crs = 26916)+
  theme_minimal()
```
```{r}
chi_bnb_data <- bnb_sample_sf |> 
  filter(city == "Chicago") |> 
  st_transform(26916) 
```
```{r}
chi_model <- lm(log(price) ~ room_type + bedrooms + review_scores_rating + has_pool, data = chi_bnb_data) 
```
```{r}
summary(chi_model)
```

```{r}
extracted_values<- extract(raster, chi_bnb_data)
chi_bnb_data$kde_value <- extracted_values[,2]
```


```{r}
chi_model_2 <- lm(log(price) ~ room_type + accommodates + bathrooms + bedrooms+ review_scores_rating+ has_pool + kde_value, data = chi_bnb_data) 
```




```{r}
chi_model_2 |> summary()
plot(chi_model_2, which = 1, add.smooth = F, id.n = 0 )
plot(chi_model_2, which = 2, id.n = 0)
```
```{r}
chi_model_2 |> 
 vif()
```

The variable `has_pool` is no longer significant when using `kde_value`. This could be because Airbnbs with pools were already in neighborhoods closer to downtown, and the KDE can explain this variation. 

```{r}
chi_model_3 <- lm(log(price) ~ room_type + accommodates + bathrooms + bedrooms+ review_scores_rating+ has_pool + kde_value + neighbourhood, data = chi_bnb_data) 
```
```{r}
summary(chi_model_3)
```

While introducing neighborhood dummies increased the multiple $R^2$ from 0.608 to 0.677, the Adjusted $R^2$ did not change by much (0.601 to 0.613) while adding all of the neighborhoods. Moreover, multiple sparse neighborhoods yielded observations with leverage = 1, signaling overfitting, and nearly 20% of the observations have been deleted due to missing data. Lastly, the `neighbourhood` predictor is specific to Chicago, whereas `kde_value` can be computed for any city. Therefore, the KDE model will be used.
